# An oriented mixed-volume cap bound with an exact pyramid remainder

This is a scalar replacement for one part of the failed higher-dimensional section-body containment. It uses the ACTUAL cap subsets and the orientation of their section measure. It is sharp on the homothetic centroid caps of every simplex. The anisotropic cube certificate shows exactly why its mixed-volume term alone cannot supply a dimension-only depth constant.

The containment failures are proved in `candidate 455c254ad09b8374`. The new argument here is elementary pyramid inclusion; it is not a consequence of treating Blaschke addition as Minkowski addition. For notation only, the mixed-volume representation and Minkowski's first inequality are in Sections 5--6 of [R. J. Gardner, The Brunn--Minkowski inequality](https://sites.stat.washington.edu/jaw/COURSES/520s/523/HO.523.20/Gardner.BullAMS.02.pdf).

## 1. Actual caps, section measure and mixed-volume convention

Let B be a positive convex d-body, d>=2, and g an interior point. Let theta_j>0 sum to one and let

    H_j={X:u_j.(X-g)>=0},   |u_j|=1,
    D_j=B intersect H_j,
    F_j=B intersect {u_j.(X-g)=0},
    s_j=H^(d-1)(F_j).

All cuts are proper. Assume the weighted original-boundary cap trace has normal marginal beta S_B. Since the cut planes pass through g, the divergence formula also gives

    sum_j theta_j |D_j|=beta |B|.                   (1)

For a critical equal-mass cap law this is the original beta, with |D_j|=beta|B| separately. The proof below only needs (1).

Define the oriented section measure

    R=sum_j theta_j s_j delta_(-u_j).

Assume R is the surface-area measure of a positive body J; alternatively retain R itself in all displayed integrals. The relevant mixed volume is

    V_1(J,B)=V(J[d-1],B)
            =(1/d) integral h_(B-g)(v) dS_J(v).

The arbitrary translation of B is harmless because R has zero first moment. Reflection gives

    V_1(-J,B)=(1/d)sum_j theta_j s_j h_(B-g)(u_j),
    V_1(J,B) =(1/d)sum_j theta_j s_j h_(B-g)(-u_j). (2)

The order of the mixed-volume arguments matters: J is repeated d-1 times.

## 2. The actual pyramid inclusion and sharp inequality

Choose a farthest captured point v_j in B satisfying

    u_j.(v_j-g)=h_(B-g)(u_j)=h_j^+>0.

Convexity gives the ACTUAL inclusion

    P_j^+=conv(F_j union {v_j}) subset D_j.

This pyramid has volume s_j h_j^+/d. Define its nonnegative excess

    e_j^+=|D_j|-s_j h_j^+/d>=0.

Its volume, hence e_j^+, does not depend on the tangential choice of v_j on the far support face. Summing with (1)--(2) gives the exact identity

    beta |B|=V_1(-J,B)+sum_j theta_j e_j^+.         (3)

In particular the explicit cap-law-dependent lower bound is

    beta>=V_1(-J,B)/|B|.                            (4)

Equality holds exactly when EVERY positive-weight captured cap is the pyramid over its actual cut section with a farthest captured apex. Indeed each nonnegative excess must vanish; containment of positive convex bodies with equal volume implies equality of the bodies. This is a geometric equality condition, not an assumption of homothetic sections.

Apply the same construction to the complementary caps. If h_j^-=h_(B-g)(-u_j), then

    e_j^-=|B\D_j|-s_j h_j^-/d>=0,
    (1-beta)|B|=V_1(J,B)+sum_j theta_j e_j^-.        (5)

Boundary hyperplanes have zero d-volume, so the closed/open convention on the complement does not affect this identity. The two bounds have different directions as statements about beta: (4) is a lower bound, while (5) gives beta<=1-V_1(J,B)/|B|. They cannot be added as if they were two lower bounds.

## 3. A volume corollary and its cap-law factor

Minkowski's first inequality gives

    V_1(-J,B)>=|J|^((d-1)/d)|B|^(1/d).

Consequently

    beta>=(|J|/|B|)^((d-1)/d).                     (6)

The sharper oriented factor is

    alpha(B,J)=V_1(-J,B)/[|J|^((d-1)/d)|B|^(1/d)]>=1,

so (4) is alpha(B,J) times the right side of (6). The factor depends on the actual oriented section law through J. Replacing it by one discards information, and equality in (6) additionally requires -J and B homothetic.

These statements do not presume a universal upper or lower bound on J's diameter. They remain meaningful on the anisotropic boxes that invalidate the containment route.

## 4. Exact sharp simplex calibration

For a d-simplex, take the d+1 equal-weight vertex caps through its centroid. Put N=d+1 and r=d/N. The preceding obstruction source computed

    beta=r^d,
    J=sB,  s=r N^(-1/(d-1)),
    s^(d-1)=r^(d-1)/N.

For a centered simplex, the support in the direction opposite any original facet normal is d times its support in that facet normal. Therefore

    V_1(-J,B)=d s^(d-1)|B|=r^d |B|=beta|B|.

Every captured cap is itself precisely the pyramid in Section 2, so all e_j^+ vanish. Bound (4) is EXACTLY sharp at Gamma_d. In contrast

    V_1(J,B)=s^(d-1)|B|=beta|B|/d,
    alpha(B,J)=d.

Thus the crude volume corollary (6) is smaller than the sharp value by factor d on this very calibration. This is why retaining orientation rather than just Blaschke volume matters.

The complementary excesses generally do not vanish. No equality in both (3) and (5) is inferred from simplex sharpness.

## 5. Exact anisotropic cube test and the missing quantitative input

For the unit cube and the weighted coordinate halfcaps from the obstruction source, beta=1/2 and

    R has mass w_i/2 at each of +/-e_i,
    h_(B-g)(+/-e_i)=1/2.

Hence for EVERY positive weight choice, including arbitrarily anisotropic section bodies,

    V_1(J,B)=V_1(-J,B)=1/(2d),
    sum_j theta_j e_j^+
       =sum_j theta_j e_j^-=(d-1)/(2d).             (7)

The identities can also be checked cap by cap: a halfcube has volume 1/2, while its section has area one and its far support height is 1/2, so its inscribed pyramid has volume 1/(2d). Thus (4)--(6) are valid on the actual counterexample, but (4) is weak by factor d there.

In particular a proposed universal bound V_1(-J,B)>=Gamma_d|B| is FALSE: (7) gives 1/(2d)<Gamma_d for d>=2. The exact criticality and full normal-convex stress of the cube do not change this calculation. The nonnegative excess in (3) contains actual geometric information absent from R; it cannot simply be discarded if one seeks a sharp dimension-only result.

The new proved conclusion is the sharp cap-law-dependent scalar bound (4), its exact positive remainder, and its equality classification. Inferring a universal lower bound for the sum in (3) would require a separate geometric argument. Rewriting that sum as beta is not progress and is not claimed here.

The checker `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_oriented_section_mixed_volume_cone_bound_slab_recovery.py` verifies the exact simplex/cube coefficients and rational pyramid-volume examples. The inequality itself is proved by the actual convex inclusion in Section 2.
